The §7 catalog contract test. Fails when a default/checkpoint test file has no catalog entry, when two entries claim one named acceptance lock, when a generating gate lacks an isolated output declaration, when a protected-output gate — or a SUITE that would run one — is assigned unsafe parallel execution, or when README disagrees with the catalog. Each condition is proved by a forced failure so the check is never green for the wrong reason. Suite membership is derived from the command, not trusted from gate_ids, and file discovery is recursive.

new_findings.evidence: Review of PR #25 found that suite.full_python_inventory declared gate_ids: [] and serial_required: false while its command, `pytest tests/`, collects py.test_verify_workbook_candidate — a gate this same catalog marks hashes_protected_roots: true. The serial check read only gate_ids, so an empty list satisfied it for any serial_required value, and the condition-4 mutation only flipped a gate's serial_group, never a suite's.
new_findings.classification: A live misclassification plus an unenforced §7 condition 4 at suite level — the exact 'a check only observed passing is not a check' failure mode this catalog exists to prevent, in the catalog's own contract test.
new_findings.action: Fixed in this checkpoint. Both full-inventory suites now declare complete membership, the Python inventory is serial, membership is derived from the command and must match the declaration, and two forced mutations cover the suite-level case. Generating gates may no longer declare in_process or read_only isolation, and generates / hashes_protected_roots are required fields.

modeling_notes: No gate declares intentional_product_acceptance_lock as its PRIMARY authority. Locks attach to gates through the acceptance_locks field and are tracked as behaviors in the coverage ledger. stingray-form-regression owns the dealer lock but its dominant job is runtime state, so that is what it declares. When Checkpoint 1 splits the dealer lock out of that 2,949-line file, the split-out owner should declare the lock class directly. Deliberate choice, recorded so a later reader does not read it as an omission.

Two of the six documented stale assertions have SIBLING assertions in the same test encoding the same superseded decision: stingray-form-regression.test.mjs:2859 and z06-runtime-rule-corrections.test.mjs:238. Those siblings currently PASS, which makes them the dangerous ones — a rewrite that fixes only the failing line leaves the superseded behavior pinned.

approximate_seconds is wall time for one process per gate. A single pytest invocation over several files is faster than the sum, because interpreter startup and workbook import are paid once. Compare like with like before claiming an improvement.
